open_issues: No test covers the four Windows probes themselves (WindowsWordProbe registry mapping, WiaScannerProbe COM enumeration, WindowsDiskSpaceProbe, WindowsRuntimeProbe). tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests targets net10.0 and cannot reference the net10.0-windows WPF host, and creating a tests/Wakeel.Desktop.Tests project would need a new entry in Wakeel.slnx, which this package may not edit. The probes' consumers are fully covered through IWordProbe/IScannerProbe/IDiskSpaceProbe/IRuntimeProbe fakes, and all four were exercised for real by the live host boot. WindowsWordProbe.DescribeVersion is deliberately internal static so it is ready to test the moment such a project exists.

ReminderScheduler.Start(IMinuteTicker) is wired but nothing in the running host starts it yet: ReminderScheduler and IBadgeService are Scoped (they need WakeelDb, which only exists after sign-in), so the tick has to be started by the shell once a session is open. That belongs to the B2 screens package (the W08/W10 shell), not to Core; App.xaml.cs only registers the types. Same for IClockGuard.StartAsync, which the shell must call at sign-in.

notifications has no unique index on `source`, where the reminder idempotency key is stored. Idempotency is enforced in the service (pre-load the pass's keys, then check-then-insert), which is sound for this app's single writer per database, but a second concurrent writer could in principle duplicate a reminder. Adding the index means editing Migrations/0001_initial.sql, which would change the schema under every other package mid-build, so it was not done.

BadgeKeys repeats the sidebar item/group key strings from WSidebar.Keys in Wakeel.Design, because Core sits below the design library and cannot reference it. A test asserting the two lists stay identical belongs in tests/Wakeel.UI.Tests (which can see both) and is outside this package's allowed paths — it is called out in BadgeKeys' XML doc.
notes:
MEASUREMENTS (the spec's 200 ms budget on 10k mixed rows). Seeded 10,000 rows (3000 correspondence, 3000 tasks, 1500 commitments, 1000 cases, 1000 decisions, 500 phone expenses; 10% late / 10% near / 10% stale per table, 3-in-5 expenses pending). Median of 5 warm runs: attention snapshot 51 ms, badge refresh 54 ms, attention counts 43 ms. Seeding itself 1516 ms. DailyShellPerformanceTests prints these on every run so head-room is visible from the output, and a companion test asserts the services' counts equal the seeder's known totals exactly — speed with a wrong answer would pass otherwise.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS. (1) The four attention buckets are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, classified pending-confirmation -> late -> near -> stale. Otherwise an overdue, long-untouched task would be both «متأخر» and «راكد», the four KPI numbers would not add up to the list beneath them, and the row would show on two W09 tabs. (2) Item 26 is implemented literally: each sidebar item's badge counts DISTINCT records pending for it, and each group header is the size of the UNION of its items' record sets, not the sum of their badges. This matters because «مركز الانتباه» deliberately contains what the other daily-work items contain; a test crafts six records whose item badges sum to 11 and asserts the header shows 6. Records are identified as (table, id). (3) BadgeService reads through ONE attention pass (IAttentionService.GetAllAsync) and slices the buckets in memory — asking per bucket would re-run the same six queries four times. (4) Reminder idempotency uses a per-event key reminder:<kind>:<id>:<slot> in notifications.source; the slot is the exact fire instant for meetings/appointments/due dates and the DAY for the item-52 cycle reminders, which is what makes «يوميًا حتى الإصدار» repeat daily while a meeting never repeats. A pass pre-loads used keys once, so round-trips do not grow with due events, and a 12-hour lookback means a sleeping machine raises a reminder late rather than losing it. (5) ClockGuard blocks numbering on Suspect as well as Bad — an official number carries a date — and «تجاهل مؤقتًا» is memory-only and never unblocks numbering; an Ok check clears the dismissal, and an Import that finds a problem re-shows the banner (new evidence, not the complaint the user waved away). (6) Core's Arabic lives in ONE file, src/Wakeel.Core/Services/CoreAr.cs, with the reasoning in it: §12 puts UI strings in Wakeel.Design/Text/Ar.*.cs, but Core is referenced BY Design and cannot reference it, while the spec requires Core to emit finished Arabic (health messages, notification titles, quick-capture toasts). Every number goes through InvariantCulture so digits stay ASCII even under ar-SA — a test sets CurrentCulture to ar-SA and asserts no Arabic-Indic digits appear. (7) HealthService never throws: each of the 11 cards is produced in its own try/catch, so a probe exception becomes a card, not a failed render. The vault card samples the newest 200 indexed documents (existence + size vs documents.size) plus the folder's file count, and says so — full verification is B6's. (8) Quick-capture undo soft-deletes (official records are never hard-deleted); tokens are opaque, single-use and expire after 2 minutes, and an expense's undo also soft-deletes its two ledger lines so the book balance goes back.

TWO BUGS FOUND AND FIXED BY THE TESTS. ClockGuard.Apply compared whole ClockBannerState records, so StateChanged fired on every ten-minute re-check because only the timestamp had changed — it now compares only what the user can see or do. QuickCaptureService.CaptureExpenseAsync wrote the transaction and its ledger lines in one SaveChanges; WakeelDb deliberately configures no navigations, so EF ordered the ledger inserts first and the FOREIGN KEY failed — it now does two saves inside one database transaction and respects a transaction the caller already opened.

HOST FIDELITY. Wakeel.Desktop.exe ran on port 9333 with an empty temp --data-folder; /json/version answered, /json/list reported /first-run. The CDP screenshot was looked at: W02 renders intact in dark RTL — «مرحبًا بك في التشغيل الأول», the three-step indicator with step 2 active, the «ملف الإعداد» card with drop zone, «كلمة مرور الحزمة» with the reveal eye, «فحص الحزمة», the signed-package notice, footer «الوكيل v0.21 — 16/09/2026 20:24». No server, port, internet or database wording on screen. Host log held exactly one line ("Wakeel desktop host starting up"), no errors; the process was killed and zero Wakeel.Desktop.exe remained. This package builds no screens (B2's screens are a separate package), so there is no other screen-by-screen fidelity to report.

No NuGet package was added; nothing outside the allowed paths was edited — the Wakeel.Design / Wakeel.UI / E2E / UI.Tests / Walkthrough modifications visible in git status were already in the tree from the b2-carryover work before this package started.
